description: This study uses a recently developed model to analyse how geomagnetically induced currents affect railway signalling track circuits in the United Kingdom during the March 1989 and October 2003 geomagnetic storms, with the 1989 storm scaled to estimate 1-in-100 and 1-in-200 year extremes. It models the Glasgow to Edinburgh line and the Preston to Lancaster section of the West Coast Main Line. No right-side failures (unoccupied sections shown occupied) are suggested for either historical storm and potential wrong-side failures (occupied sections shown clear) are few, but both are possible on both routes in the extreme storms, with more on the Glasgow to Edinburgh line and most within 2 to 3 hours either side of the peak. Coverage: two British lines. Format and access: open access article in Scientific Reports (2024) on PubMed Central. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: modelled results; the article record read lists no separate data deposit. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies of signalling under space weather. It relates to the Lloyd's extreme space weather scenario and the 1989 Hydro-Québec and 2003 Malmö blackouts in the catalogue.
